newsitem.title: USA: CSCE says to look into Colombian coffee forecast.
newsitem.headline: CSCE says to look into Colombian coffee forecast.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) said late on Wednesday it planned to look into the circumstances surrounding reports carried by wire services on February 26 that the National Federation of Coffee Growers of Colombia had issued a substantially lower 1996/97 crop estimate compared with its previous forecast.

During trading hours on Wednesday, a spokesman from Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation estimated the country's 1996/97 coffee crop could come in at about 8.3 million 60-kg bags, well below the most recent estimate of 10.4 million bags.
Spokesman Roman Medina gave no immediate explanation for the sharp downward revision in less than one week.

Within one-half hour of the release, the Federation reiterated that its previous forecast of 10.4 million bags, made last week, still stands. A spokesman said today's lower forecast had been based on an erroneous calculation.
CSCE coffee prices came reeling off new life-of-contract highs after the Federation retracted the 8.3 million bag forecast and the 10.4 million bag estimate was confirmed as correct.
At the close Wednesday, most-active May coffee stood at 172.85 cents per lb, up 9.60 cents on the day, but well off the new contract high of 177.00 cents.
The Exchange said it would ask the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to work with them on the matter.
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk, 212 859 1640
